chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, may Allah be pleased with him, wrote to Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who died while ten days of missed fasts from the month of Ramaḍān remained upon him, and he had two heirs: is it permissible for them both to make them up on his behalf together, one of the two heirs fasting five days and the other five days?
So he عليه السلام wrote in reply: “The elder of his two heirs should make up ten days on his behalf consecutively, if Allah wills.”

key_terms.أَكْبَرُ وَلِيَّيْهِ: the elder of his two heirs, designated here for the duty
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramaḍān, whose missed fasts are under discussion
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: make-up performance of an owed religious duty
key_terms.وَلِيَّانِ: two heirs or legal representatives of the deceased
key_terms.وِلَاءً: consecutively, one after another without interruption

ai.seo_question: Who should make up the missed Ramaḍān fasts of a deceased person when he has two heirs?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning missed fasts owed by a deceased person. It states that when there are two heirs, the eldest heir is to perform the full ten days of make-up fasting consecutively on behalf of the deceased, by the will of Allah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2010 - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, may Allah (swt) be pleased with him, wrote to Imam Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Ali (as):

Regarding a man who passed away and had ten days of fasting left from the Month of Ramadan, and he had two heirs. Is it permissible for both heirs to divide the days, with each fasting five days on his behalf?
The Imam (as) replied in writing: "The eldest of the two heirs should fast all ten days consecutively, if Allah (swt) wills."
